title: Micropatterned Surfaces to Study Hyaluronic Acid Interactions with Cancer Cells
protocol: Rinse a new silicon wafer with ethanol.
Dry the wafer with a stream of air.
Handle the wafer with forceps to prevent surface defects throughout the process.
Transfer the wafer to a spin coater.
Cover at least 80% of the wafer's surface with SU-2025 negative photoresist.
Spin coat for 10 seconds at 600 rpm, followed by 30 seconds at 3000 rpm.
Place the photoresist-coated silicon wafer on a hot plate for "soft-bake" at 95°C for 3 minutes.
Allow the wafer to cool for 1 minute after removing it from the hot plate.
Place a pre-fabricated mask with the desired pattern onto the photoresist-covered silicon wafer and expose to ultraviolet (UV) irradiation (350-450 nm) for 20 seconds.
Transfer the silicon wafer to a hot plate for "hard-bake" at 110°C for 6 minutes.
Carefully rinse the silicon wafer with SU-8 photoresist developer solution.
Rinse the wafer three times with the developer solution and then rinse with ethanol.
If any white residue is present, repeat the rinse process with photoresist developer or submerge in developer solution for 2 minutes before rinsing with ethanol again.
Wash the silicon wafer with water and air dry.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer solution and curing agent in a 10:1 weight ratio.
Centrifuge at 900rpm for 5 minutes to remove air bubbles.
Place patterned wafer in Petri dish and pour PDMS onto silicon wafer.
If there are bubbles present, place in desiccator and vacuum for a couple of minutes until bubbles disappear.
Cure overnight at room temperature (RT) to form a complementary elastomeric stamp.
If PDMS is not completely cured after 12 hours, place in oven at 60°C for 30 minutes.
Carefully remove PDMS from silicon wafer.
Use a razor edge to cut stamp to desired size.
Sonicate in ethanol for 15 minutes.
Plasma clean glass slides for 5 minutes.
Place all slides into chamber and vacuum for 5 minutes.
Allow low flow of oxygen to enter chamber.
Turn plasma cleaner on for 5 minutes.
Remove from plasma cleaner and place in a Petri dish using forceps.
During plasma cleaning, sonicate PDMS stamps in ethanol for 15 minutes.
Prepare a fresh 3% v/v solution of 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane (APTMS) in 95% v/v ethanol in a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Allow to react for 5 minutes at RT to form a silanol.
Place PDMS stamp pattern-up on spin coater chuck and cover patterned surface with APTMS solution.
Spincoat at 3500rpm for 30 seconds.
Transfer APTMS solution to plasma-cleaned glass surfaces using PDMS stamp facing down.
Glide pressing PDMS on the patterned side of the glass surface for 1 minute.
Remove PDMS stamp gently and allow patterned glass slide to incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Rinse patterned surfaces with ethanol and air dry.
Sonicate PDMS stamp for 15 minutes to remove excess APTMS.
Heat patterned glass slides in an oven or on a hot plate for 1 hour at 115°C.
Rinse heated patterns with ethanol and dry with air.
Prepare fresh polyethylene glycol (PEG)-silane solution of 20% v/v 2-[methoxy(polyethyleneoxy)propyl] trimethoxysilane in toluene.
Transfer patterned glass slide to a glass Petri dish and incubate in PEG-silane solution for 45 minutes at 75°C on a hot plate.
Rinse with toluene, water, and dry with air.
Sterilize the treated slides using UV germicidal irradiation in a biological safety cabinet for 1 hour.
Proceed in a biological safety cabinet from this point forward to maintain sterility.
Prepare aqueous sterile hyaluronic acid (HA) solution containing 10mM of 1-Ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC), 5mM of N-hydroxysuccinimide, and 50 μg/mL fluorescein-labeled HA.
Apply the HA solution to the patterned glass substrates in sterile conditions and protected from light.
Allow patterned substrates to remain undisturbed for 16-24 hours.
Aspirate off HA solution.
Wash surface with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Cover surface with 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS for 1 hour.

Seed single cell suspensions of MDA-MB-231 human breast cancer cells and LS174T colorectal carcinoma cells onto HA immobilized surfaces according to the manufacturer's instructions, using densities between 0.4 and 1x10^6 cancer cells per 18.75 cm² glass surface area.
Incubate in humidified incubator (37 °C) with atmospheres maintained at 5% CO2.
Change media every other day.
Observe cell adhesion using inverted light microscope after 24 hours.
Maintain cell culture surfaces up to 5 days under standard incubator conditions.
Analyze cellular responses on HA surface using additional assays as needed.
